To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CD8 T‐cell compartment is persistently elevated in HIV infection and that the elevation is associated with an increased risk for non-AIDS events.

the CD8 T‐cell compartment is persistently altered during HIV infection and this is associated with a disturbed homeostasis of the CD8 compartment, a persistent elevation of T‐cell activation and a persistent elevation in the frequency of CD8 T-cell subsets that are enriched for HIV-specific T-cells.
the CD8 compartment in HIV infection is not a static entity, but is dynamic, characterized by a progressive elevation of the CD8 compartment over time, which persists in ART-treated individuals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What is the role of the CD8 T‐cell compartment during HIV infection and what is the impact of antiretroviral treatment (ART) on this compartment?
the following questions: (i) What are the mechanisms that lead to CD8 T‐cell elevation in HIV infection?
understanding the role of the CD8 T‐cell compartment in HIV infection and its potential as a biomarker for disease progression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CD8 T‐cell elevation is a consequence of the disease and not a cause of it.
CD8 T‐cell elevation is a hallmark of chronic HIV infection.
CD8 T‐cell elevation is not a good prognostic factor, but that CD8 T-cell persistence in the ART era is.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIV‐induced changes in CD8 T‐cell homeo­stasis are not a mere consequence of CD4 T cell loss, but are a major driver for disease progression.
HIV infection leads to an expansion of CD8 T cells, which are not exhausted, but rather persist and expand in the absence of CD4 T cell help, leading to a chronic immune activation and inflammation.
the CD8 T‐cell elevation in HIV infection is not only a consequence of the HIV infection itself, but also a major contributor to HIV‐associated disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that

CD8 T-cytopenia is a common phenomenon, and is a major determinant for the development of immune reconstitution inflammatory disease (IRIS), which is the main complication of ART initiation in the acute phase of HIV infection.
the CD8 T-cell compartment is not only a bystander, but rather an important driver of HIV‐related immunodeficiency and disease progression.
the CD8 compartment in HIV infection is characterized by a high turnover and an elevated persistence, which is maintained in the ART era.
